implementation_notes: Diesel declares the association as an attribute on the child struct (#[diesel(belongs_to(User))]) while the child stores user_id and both sides derive Identifiable; the query API then exposes Post::belonging_to(&user) plus grouped_by to batch children with their parents. Diesel deliberately has no has_many: data and associations are kept separate, which trades an object-navigation API for explicit queries without N+1-by-default. sqlx and SeaORM are the alternatives (runtime-checked SQL / entity relations); hand-written mapping over rusqlite remains justified when you want no query DSL and ownership of every statement.
code_sketch:
#[derive(Identifiable, Queryable, Associations)]
#[diesel(belongs_to(User))]
#[diesel(table_name = posts)]
struct Post { id: i32, user_id: i32, title: String }

let posts = Post::belonging_to(&user).load::<Post>(&mut conn)?;  // key resolved by query
pitfalls: There is no has_many: the parent does not own its children, so grouping must be explicit (grouped_by) or the N+1 returns through a per-parent query.
belongs_to(Foo) needs Foo in scope and the conventional foreign key name (table_name_id); a renamed column compiles and then fails at query time.
Lifetime-bearing records need '_ in the attribute (belongs_to(User<'_>)) until unrestricted attribute tokens land, and the parent borrow must outlive the query.
